mechanism: On workday mornings, occupancy is dominated by the regular commute, so historical workday morning segments should be most informative.
activation_condition: when hour_of_day is morning and working_day is workday
failure_condition: public holidays, school holidays, or non-recurring incidents disrupt the commute pattern
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to the same hour-of-day window and prefer workday historical segments.
expected_effect: Retrieved futures will reflect the recurrent morning peak level and shape instead of mixing in off-peak or weekend dynamics.
reason: Commute demand has strong hour-of-day and working-day regularity, so matching these calendar conditions should reduce irrelevant historical variation.

notes: retrieval_action subsumed by activation scope; no additional executable transform

mechanism: High recent volatility signals a fast-changing regime, so the closest available historical window is more reliable than distant volatility-matched segments.
failure_condition: the volatility spike is caused by a one-off incident that is resolved before the forecast horizon
retrieval_action: Retrieve short-lag historical segments immediately preceding the current window instead of selecting by volatility similarity.
expected_effect: The retrieved futures will better reflect the current unstable dynamics and reduce mixing with stale stable periods.
reason: In high-volatility regimes, recent history dominates, so a short lag aligns retrieval with current shocks rather than attempting unreliable volatility matching.
claim: High recent volatility signals a fast-changing regime, so the closest available historical window is more reliable than distant volatility-matched segments.

retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to the same hour-of-day and prefer the same working-day type instead of matching recent_level.
expected_effect: Retrieved futures will capture off-peak scheduling regularities without duplicating the harmful low-level matching signal.
reason: Low occupancy episodes are often tied to time-of-day and day type, so calendar structure provides a more robust retrieval basis than absolute level similarity.

reason: The current rate of change contains information about the immediate direction and speed of demand evolution.

expected_effect: Retrieved futures will match the characteristic evening peak shape and workday travel demand.
reason: Evening demand differs from morning because trip purposes and timing dispersion differ, so both hour-of-day and working-day matching are needed.
